newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS RULED OUT OF DAVIS CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS RULED OUT OF DAVIS CUP TIE.

text.p: Australia's hopes of upsetting holders France in the Davis Cup first round next month suffered a blow on Tuesday when top singles player Mark Philippoussis was ruled out because of injury.

Philippoussis has failed to recover from the tendinitis in his right forearm that forced his withdrawal before the start of this month's Australian Open in Melbourne, Australia Davis Cup captain John Newcombe said.
Sandon Stolle was called into the squad as Philippoussis' replacement to face the French on grass at White City in Sydney.
"It was too risky to try Philippoussis' arm (in a) best-of-five set matches on grass," Newcombe said.

"You go out and try to play too early on an arm injury and it could put you out for a long time. He's obviously pretty disappointed but he's just hoping that it's not something that's going to linger," Newcombe said.
Stolle, ranked 52 in the world, joined Pat Rafter and doubles specialists Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge in the squad for the match between February 7-9.
Jason Stoltenberg, a semifinalist on grass at last year's Wimbledon, is also unavailable for the tie because of a wrist injury.
"I think this match is a really honest 50-50 call," Newcombe said. "France are the defending champions -- they're going to fight like tigers to protect that."
France, who beat Sweden 3-2 to win the Davis Cup last month, will choose their four-man team from Guy Forget, Cedric Pioline, Arnaud Boetsch, Guillaume Raoux and Lionel Roux.
